title: Machine Learning Modeling
text:
Evaluation design
A future experiment should pin the same source manifest as the explorer, report posting records and employer groups separately, and split employers between training, validation and test sets to avoid reusing the same employer across splits. Case-folded company names are only an approximate grouping key.
Evaluate NAICS 4, 5 and 6 separately, including per-class support, missing-label exclusions, macro-F1 and confusion counts. Choose model settings using validation data and report the held-out test result once. A broad parent code must not be promoted to a detailed training label without supporting industry evidence.
Inspect the current full-data industry counts.

title: Job Postings Research
text:
Understand the evidence
Posting records count source rows, including repeated advertisements. Employer counts count distinct normalized company names and are not a count of jobs. Employers can appear in several industries. Training samples belong to a separate modeling experiment; this explorer does not train or evaluate a classifier.
The Data Exploration page explains coverage and verification. The Modeling page defines how a future classifier should be evaluated separately from existing source labels.
The website publishes aggregates only. Raw source data remains in the dataset folders.

title: Industry explorer
text:
What the counts mean

Posting records: rows in the full US snapshot, with duplicate advertisements retained. These are not independently deduplicated vacancies or a count of currently live jobs.
Distinct employer names: non-placeholder company names, normalized for capitalization and whitespace. They are not verified legal entities. One employer can appear in several industries, so employer counts must not be added across rows.
Model training sample: no training sample is used in this explorer. It describes existing labels across the complete snapshot and does not report predictive accuracy.
Coverage: populated codes of the expected numeric length. Counts overlap across NAICS levels. A populated classification is not independent verification of an employer or worksite industry.

Industry codes and titles are stored separately. The website displays the source NAICS 2022 title; conflicting title variants, if present, remain counted in the download’s title_variants column.
